articles.title: Hackers pretended to be technical support in Teams and took control of computers
articles.excerpt: Attackers combined Microsoft Teams social engineering with Quick Assist and AD CS misconfigurations (such as ESC1 and ESC8) to obtain privileged certificates. Without a software patch available, secur…
articles.body: Attackers combined Microsoft Teams social engineering with Quick Assist and AD CS misconfigurations (such as ESC1 and ESC8) to obtain privileged certificates. Without a software patch available, security relies on configuration hardening and restricting external tenants. According to a Microsoft report, the attackers did not exploit any technical issues or vulnerabilities in the Teams application itself. Instead, they relied on people being tricked and misconfigured in companies' identity and certificate management systems. How the attacks started The attackers contacted employees via Teams messages and calls, posing as internal technical support. They used external accounts with support-related names to appear familiar to the victims.

articles.title: How to Learn Big O Notation (and Stop Freezing When Someone Asks for the Complexity)
articles.excerpt: The first time an interviewer asked me "what's the time complexity of that?", I said "O(n)" with total confidence. It was O(n²). I had a loop inside a loop and didn't see it, because I'd learned Big O…
articles.body: The first time an interviewer asked me "what's the time complexity of that?", I said "O(n)" with total confidence. It was O(n²). I had a loop inside a loop and didn't see it, because I'd learned Big O as a list of symbols and not as a way of counting. I'd read the explainer posts. I'd seen the chart with the curves bending up and away. I could recite that binary search is O(log n). What I couldn't do was look at my own code and work it out. If that sounds familiar, here's the approach that finally fixed it for me. Big O is just counting, roughly Forget the math notation for a minute. Big O answers one question: if the input gets 10 times bigger, how much more work does this code do? If the work grows 10 times, it's O(n). If it grows 100 times, it's O(n²).

In the LiveCodeBench Hard benchmark, this “team‑solve” strategy outperformed Meta’s Fable‑5 , a state‑of‑the‑art code‑generation model. Memdoor shows that orchestrating multiple smaller models can be more effective than a single monolithic model.

articles.title: Multi-user KDE Plasma over RDP on a headless server: running Plasma inside sway
articles.excerpt: KDE Plasma has an RDP server, KRdp. It is good, but it does one thing: it shares a session that is already running on a machine with a screen. If you have a server and want every user to log in over R…
articles.body: KDE Plasma has an RDP server, KRdp. It is good, but it does one thing: it shares a session that is already running on a machine with a screen. If you have a server and want every user to log in over RDP and get their own Plasma desktop, kept alive between connections, KRdp does not do that. Plasma also cannot start on a headless machine: KWin wants a monitor. I work on Waydesk , a free multi-user RDP desktop server for Linux (Debian, Ubuntu and Arch), and I wanted Plasma to be one of the desktops an account can choose. This is how it works, what it costs and what I have not tested. Why not just use KRdp? KRdp is built to share the session of someone sitting at a machine: one user, one running desktop, a monitor attached. That is the right design for remote support.

articles.title: What is Starshield? A look at SpaceX's military satellite network
articles.excerpt: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them?
articles.body: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated.

articles.title: 'Metroid Prime' needs some 'Resident Evil'-style remakes to rediscover its sci-fi shooter mojo
articles.excerpt: Nintendo's sci-fi shooter franchise is in dire straits, but we've got the solution to Samus's problems.
articles.body: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was, unfortunately, not the return many were hoping for when it finally arrived on Nintendo Switch consoles in 2025. After five years in development at Retro Studios, the original makers of the Metroid Prime series, fans were greeted with annoying side characters, a bike for Samus to roam the barren landscape on, and a deeply unsatisfying ending. It’s a shame, considering how beloved the Metroid Prime series has been since the first title’s 2002 debut for the Nintendo GameCube. Many franchises were jumping from 2D to 3D at the turn of the millennium, and there were plenty of failures — but Metroid wasn’t one of them.

articles.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks
articles.excerpt: Satellites are watching fireballs blaze through Earth's atmosphere, strengthening planetary defense knowhow and helping scientists learn more about space debris impacts.
articles.body: It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
